title: Accessing allocated memory safely and checking allocation results
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its C rules.
Trace the example and identify data or resource flow.
Recognize relevant safety and failure cases.
Apply the concept in a tested C program.

understand.concept: After a successful allocation, the program may access only the allocated object region and must respect alignment, effective type and lifetime rules. Every element should be initialized before its value is read. Allocation failure must be handled before dereferencing the returned pointer.
understand.whyItMatters: A successful allocation gives storage, not automatically initialized application data. Safe access requires both a valid allocation and correct bounds.
understand.analogy: Treat each object or stream as a resource with a defined lifetime and explicit rules for access.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's formal object, storage-duration, alignment or library rules.

explain.narrative:
After a successful allocation, the program may access only the allocated object region and must respect alignment, effective type and lifetime rules. Every element should be initialized before its value is read. Allocation failure must be handled before dereferencing the returned pointer.

Check all allocation, I/O and conversion results. Respect object bounds and lifetime, initialize data before reading it, and define who owns and releases each resource.
